quizName:
DMV Practice Test  #5
										  					
  

30 Questions • Passing Score 24

questions.question: What driving technique helps avoid crashes on icy or snowy roads?

options.text: Add extra weight to your vehicle for better traction.
Leave the highways as quickly as possible.
Use four-wheel drive on your vehicle.
Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down and stay farther behind other cars.
questions.explanation: Slow down on snow or ice. Slowing down and increasing your distance from other cars are the best ways to avoid crashes in bad weather.

questions.question: When must you always use your turn signal?

options.text: When changing lanes.
When pulling into or out of a parking space.
When entering traffic from a parking area or alley.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Use your turn signal whenever you move left or right. Signal when leaving a parking space, changing lanes, or passing another vehicle.

questions.question: What do orange signs mean?

options.text: Work zone ahead.
Traffic rules and laws.
School zone ahead.
Directions and information.

questions.correctAnswerText: Work zone ahead.
questions.explanation: Orange signs mark work zones on highways. These diamond-shaped signs have black letters or symbols and warn you that workers are on or near the road.

questions.question: Where are stop lines painted?

options.text: On curves and hills.
Near churches and schools.
At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
On freeway entrance ramps.

questions.correctAnswerText: At intersections and pedestrian crosswalks.
questions.explanation: Stop lines are solid white lines across traffic lanes at intersections and crosswalks. They show exactly where you must stop.

questions.question: What can you do from a center turn lane?

options.text: Turn left.
Make a U-turn.
Pass slow-moving traffic.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Turn left.
questions.explanation: A center turn lane is only for left turns from either direction. You cannot use it for passing or driving straight.

questions.question: Can you drink alcohol in a vehicle on a public road?

options.text: Yes, if you are not driving.
Yes, if you sit in the back seat.
Yes, if you sit in the back of a pickup truck.
No, never.

questions.correctAnswerText: No, never.
questions.explanation: It is illegal to drink or carry open alcohol in a vehicle on any public road. This applies to all passengers and locations in the vehicle.

questions.question: Which statement is true about road lines?

options.text: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.
White lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions.
Yellow lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.
None of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: White lines separate traffic moving in the same direction.
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes moving in the same direction. Only cross white lines if they are broken.

questions.question: When can you cross a dashed white line?

options.text: Anytime.
Only during the day.
When it is safe to change lanes.
Only when passing a motorcycle.

questions.correctAnswerText: When it is safe to change lanes.
questions.explanation: Dashed white lines separate lanes moving the same direction. You can cross them to pass or change lanes if it is safe.

questions.question: What must drivers do around pedestrians?

options.text: Make sure the pedestrian sees your vehicle.
Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
Only give them the right-of-way when they have the legal right.
Slow down and honk your horn at crosswalks.

questions.correctAnswerText: Always give them the right-of-way, even if they are wrong.
questions.explanation: Do everything possible to avoid hitting a pedestrian or vehicle. It is your job to watch for pedestrians and let them cross, even if they should not be crossing there.

questions.question: What is an inattentive driver?

options.text: A driver who stares at things off the road or daydreams.
A driver who looks at a passenger while talking.
A driver who only watches the car ahead.
All of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: All of the above.
questions.explanation: Do not get distracted by passengers, items in your car, reading, sightseeing, or daydreaming. Keep watching the road, check your mirrors, and look at your instruments regularly. These safe habits will help you stay focused while driving.

questions.question: An emergency vehicle with sirens and flashing lights is directly behind you in heavy traffic. You cannot move out of the way. What should you do?

options.text: Stop where you are.
Honk your horn.
Force your way into the next lane.
Keep moving slowly until you can get out of the way.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep moving slowly until you can get out of the way.
questions.explanation: If an emergency vehicle is behind you in heavy traffic, move slowly and look for a safe place to get out of its way. You must make space for the emergency vehicle when you can.

questions.question: Traffic signals at an intersection are not working because of a power outage. What should you do?

options.text: Park your car off the road and wait for power to return.
Use hand signals to tell other drivers what you are doing.
Turn on hazard lights and go through without stopping.
Treat it like a four-way stop.

questions.correctAnswerText: Treat it like a four-way stop.
questions.explanation: When a traffic light is not working, treat the intersection as a four-way stop. Let other drivers go when it is their turn, then proceed through carefully when it is your turn.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: No right turn.
Keep right.
No U-turn.
Left lane must turn left.

questions.correctAnswerText: No right turn.
questions.explanation: This sign is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. It means you cannot turn right.

questions.question: You are in a line of traffic crossing railroad tracks with no signals or gates. What should you do?

options.text: You have the right-of-way and do not need to check for trains.
You can pass slower cars while crossing the tracks.
Make sure your car has room to cross completely without stopping.
All of the above

questions.correctAnswerText: Make sure your car has room to cross completely without stopping.
questions.explanation: Before entering the tracks, check that you have enough space to cross all the way across. Never pass another car at a railroad crossing. Always look for trains before crossing any tracks.

questions.question: Which statement about bicyclists is true?

options.text: They can ride side-by-side on roads.
They can ride two across on bike paths, unless signs say otherwise.
They have the right-of-way over people walking.
They can ride while holding onto a moving vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: They can ride two across on bike paths, unless signs say otherwise.
questions.explanation: On roads, bicyclists must ride in a single line. On bike paths or lanes that are wide enough, they may ride two across if it does not block traffic.

questions.question: How does alcohol affect your reflexes and judgment?

options.text: Beer affects you less than wine.
Wine affects you less than beer.
Hard ciders and mixed drinks affect you the most.
It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.

questions.correctAnswerText: It depends on how much alcohol is in your blood.
questions.explanation: Any type of alcohol can hurt your reflexes and judgment. The type does not matter—only the amount of alcohol in your blood.

questions.question: Traffic lanes moving in the same direction are separated by ____ lines.

options.text: Yellow
White
Red
Black

questions.correctAnswerText: White
questions.explanation: White lines separate lanes going the same direction. A solid white line means you should not cross. A broken white line means you can cross to pass. Yellow lines separate traffic going in opposite directions.

questions.question: What affects your ability to stop your car?

options.text: Traffic lights.
Other cars on the road.
What time of day it is.
The condition of the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: The condition of the road.
questions.explanation: Road condition greatly affects how well you can stop. Slow down when roads are slippery or in poor condition so you can control your car and stop safely.

questions.question: What does this sign mean?

options.text: Keep right.
Low shoulder.
No parking at any time.
Lane ends.

questions.correctAnswerText: Keep right.
questions.explanation: This is a regulation sign that tells drivers what they must do. It means you should stay to the right to avoid a hazard ahead.

questions.question: You see an emergency vehicle ahead with its lights flashing. What must you do?

options.text: Slow down. If you can, change lanes so you do not drive beside the emergency vehicle.
Move to the right side of the road and stop.
Stay in your lane and keep driving at the same speed.
Speed up to pass the vehicle quickly.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slow down. If you can, change lanes so you do not drive beside the emergency vehicle.
questions.explanation: When you see a stopped emergency vehicle with lights flashing, change lanes to give it space. If you cannot change lanes safely, slow down below the speed limit and leave as much room as possible. Always be ready to stop when you approach an emergency scene.

questions.question: What does a red arrow on a traffic light mean?

options.text: You must drive slowly through the intersection.
You must stop, then go when the way is clear.
You must stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
You may turn in the direction the red arrow points.

questions.correctAnswerText: You must stop, then go when the light turns green or a green arrow appears.
questions.explanation: A red arrow means you must come to a full stop. You must wait until the light changes to green or a green arrow appears before you go. There are no exceptions unless a sign says otherwise.

questions.question: Which of these drugs can affect your ability to drive?

options.text: Allergy medicine
Marijuana
Cold medicine
All of these

questions.correctAnswerText: All of these
questions.explanation: Many drugs can make it unsafe to drive. This includes illegal drugs, prescription drugs, and over-the-counter medicines. Driving while impaired by any drug is illegal.

questions.question: What does a single broken yellow line down the center of a two-lane road mean?

options.text: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in opposite directions. You may pass when it is safe.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You cannot pass.
Traffic moves in the same direction. You may pass when it is safe.

questions.correctAnswerText: Traffic moves in opposite directions. You may pass when it is safe.
questions.explanation: Yellow lines separate traffic moving in opposite directions. A broken yellow line means you can pass if it is safe to do so.

questions.question: When must you stop at an intersection?

options.text: When you see a flashing red light.
When you see a steady yellow light.
When you see a yellow arrow.
When you see a flashing yellow light.

questions.correctAnswerText: When you see a flashing red light.
questions.explanation: A flashing red light means the same thing as a stop sign. You must come to a complete stop, look both ways, and only go when the intersection is clear.

questions.question: You are in the right lane of a highway and want to move to the left lane. What should you do?

options.text: Check your rearview mirror for traffic behind you.
Look over your left shoulder to check your blind spot.
Check your side mirror and turn on your signal.
Do all of the above.

questions.correctAnswerText: Do all of the above.
questions.explanation: Before changing lanes, check both mirrors and look over your shoulder toward the lane you want to enter. Always use your signal when changing lanes.

questions.question: When passing a large vehicle in a small car, you should be ready for:

options.text: Loud noises.
Excess air pollution.
Strong wind from the large vehicle.
Falling vehicle parts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Strong wind from the large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Large vehicles create strong wind gusts that can push smaller vehicles off course. Be prepared to steer to stay in your lane when passing or being passed by a large vehicle.

questions.question: You want to turn left at a green light, but traffic coming toward you is heavy. What should you do?

options.text: Use the next intersection.
Wait at the crosswalk for traffic to clear.
Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
Turn because you have a green light.

questions.correctAnswerText: Wait in the center of the intersection for traffic to clear.
questions.explanation: You may enter the intersection on a green light to prepare for a left turn. But you must wait for oncoming traffic to pass before you complete the turn.

questions.question: Drivers may not pass from either side of a ____ centerline.

options.text: Combination solid and broken yellow
Single broken yellow
Double solid yellow
Single broken white

questions.correctAnswerText: Double solid yellow
questions.explanation: A double solid yellow line means no one can pass from either direction. It is illegal to cross this line to pass another vehicle.

questions.question: When turning right on a green light, you must:

options.text: Keep your normal speed.
Stop and look for police cars.
Yield to pedestrians.
Drive faster.

questions.correctAnswerText: Yield to pedestrians.
questions.explanation: On a green light, you may turn right or left unless a sign says otherwise. But you must let pedestrians and other vehicles in the intersection go first.

questions.question: How can you reduce the risk of hydroplaning?

options.text: Drive through shallow water.
Drive faster.
Drive slower.
Drive through deep water.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drive slower.
questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when you drive too fast on wet roads. Slowing down reduces the risk of hydroplaning.
